title: Two-stage Miller-compensated OTA
description: Design a two-stage operational amplifier: a first stage (an NMOS differential pair with a PMOS current-mirror load and an NMOS tail current source) providing most of the DC gain, followed by a second common-source gain stage, with a Miller compensation capacitor and RHP-zero-nulling resistor connecting the second stage's output back to its input for pole-splitting stability. Open-loop DC gain must be at least 65 dB, gain-bandwidth product at least 7 MHz, and phase margin at least 60 degrees, all across the full sky130-style tt/ss/ff process corner, 1.62-1.98 V supply, and -40..125 C temperature matrix.

target_specs.corners: sky130-style tt/ss/ff process x 1.62-1.98V supply x -40..125C

reference.notes: First stage reuses the five-transistor-ota task's own topology (see that reference's ota_5t.spice); a PMOS common-source second stage with an NMOS current-source load adds the extra gain/swing, with a Miller cap + nulling resistor for pole-splitting compensation. Open-loop gain/GBW/PM measured with the same DC-feedback-closes/AC-feedback-opens trick used across this benchmark's reference solutions -- see ota_2stage.spice's own header for why the stage-2 inversion means inp/inn are cross-connected relative to the single-stage five-transistor-ota reference. kb/entries/two-stage-miller-ota.json has no reference netlist of its own as of this task's authoring (2026-09-13) -- this is an original reference solution, not adapted from an existing KB artifact.

source.citation: P. R. Gray and R. G. Meyer, "MOS operational amplifier design-a tutorial overview," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 17, no. 6, pp. 969-982, Dec. 1982.
